arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the phantom-holder self-heal never fires — `provider.githubApi` does not exist**

The live label-layer re-read is guarded by:

```js
if (provider && typeof provider.githubApi === 'function' && repoInfo) {
    var liveData = provider.githubApi('list_prs', { owner: repoInfo.owner, repo: repoInfo.repo });
```

But the `provider` here is the facade returned by `smProviderModule.createSmProvider(...)` (githubSource.js:471-474), and that facade exposes `listOpenPrs`, `listMergedPrs`, `branchExists`, `snapshot`, `findPr`, `prStatus`, `memoPrStatus`, `merge`, `addPrLabel`, `silentUpdateBranch`, etc. — **there is no `githubApi` method anywhere in `js/common/smProvider.js`** (verified: `grep -rn "githubApi" js/ --include="*.js"` matches only these two new lines). `typeof provider.githubApi === 'function'` is therefore always `false`, `holdersLive` stays `false`, and the entire reconciliation/self-heal block below is dead code in production.

Consequence: the live incident class this PR exists to fix (phantom `ai_validating` holder deferring every candidate, AC2 — "a queued candidate arms in the SAME tick") still wedges exactly as before; only the pure-module unit tests pass because nothing stubs a production-shaped provider through this branch.

Fix: route the live re-read through a real facade surface — e.g. add `githubApi(kind, args)` (or a dedicated `listOpenPrsLive()`) to `createSmProvider`'s return object in `js/common/smProvider.js`, bypassing/refreshing the per-tick ioCache — and add a test that loads `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module shape so the guard can't silently rot again.

🚨 **BLOCKING: required `crap` quality gate is red on the head commit**

CI check `crap` failed on `1c8008e5`. The crap4js ratchet (threshold 8, baseline `crap-baseline`) reports:

```text
REGRESSION  js/factoryState.js::buildFactoryState: 65.1 -> 66.1
REGRESSION  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::queryPrs: 67.4 -> 131.8
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateFailureCount: 110
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::normalizeHolder: 36.8
NEW > 8  js/sm/sources/githubSource.js::mutexHoldersOf: 56
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::isGhostCancelProbe: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::normalizeMutexSnapshot: 20
NEW > 8  js/factoryState.js::num: 20
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::derive: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::reconcile: 13
NEW > 8  js/common/validationLiveness.js::silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12
NEW > 8  js/common/mutexRegistry.js::mergeSnapshot: 11
2 regression(s), 10 new over threshold, 0 improvement(s), 0 removed
```

The ratchet only ever goes down, so this cannot be fixed by updating the baseline — the new code must be decomposed. Concretely:

- Extract the phantom-heal block added to `queryPrs` into its own function (that block is also what drove the 67.4 → 131.8 regression, and per comment on the `githubApi` guard it is currently unreachable dead weight).
- Split `silentUpdateFailureCount` (110 — the regex-while loop plus counting makes it the worst offender), `mutexHoldersOf` (56), `normalizeHolder` (36.8), `isGhostCancelProbe` (20), `normalizeMutexSnapshot` (20, including its inner `num`).
- `silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12` is a one-liner whose score is coverage-driven — it needs a direct unit test.

The PR description's "Full suite … 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions" is true only for the unit suite; the required CRAP gate is a separate, red merge blocker.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title` and no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

```js
console.log('   ⚠️ ' + alarm.title + ' — ' + alarm.detail + ' (cached holders [' + ...);
```

So the self-heal alarm — the I2-mandated observable signal that the registry diverged — logs as `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ioCache self-healed, defer cancelled)`. The same `alarm` object is also stored in the factory-state alarm tail, so any consumer rendering `alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` (including future Q2 auto-issue filing on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks) sees the same holes.

Fix: either add `title`/`detail` to the alarm objects in `mutexRegistry.reconcile`/`recordPhantomHeal`, or log `alarm.type` (+ a human-readable phrase) here.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

Fix: include `consecutivePhantomTicks: 1` in the event (or call `recordPhantomHeal` at this site as designed), and have the publish step reset the counter to 0 when the current tick carried no phantom event.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no test exercises the new wiring — AC2/AC3 integration paths are untested**

Every hunk in this file (and in `test_smAgent.js` / `test_mergeCadence.js`) only adds `'../../common/mutexRegistry.js': loadModule(...)` to the require maps. Nothing drives a full-slot defer scenario through `queryPrs`'s new phantom-heal branch, and nothing drives `rerun_cancelled_checks`'s new ghost-cancel branch in `smAgent`.

This gap is exactly why the BLOCKING `provider.githubApi` defect slipped through: a single test loading `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module (or a stub shaped like its facade) and asserting the live re-read fires on a full-slot defer would have caught that the guard is unsatisfiable in production.

The ticket's test plan explicitly requires these hooks: IT-1 (scripted two-tick phantom self-heal → AC2), IT-2 (cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe → AC3), plus the REG-1 replay rule ("red REG blocks merge of this fix"). This PR ships only pure-function UTs of `mutexRegistry`; the scripted two-tick scenario and the REG fixture are absent. Please add at least the IT-1/IT-2 level tests against the real provider facade shape before merge.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: E3 gap — a re-cancelled re-dispatch re-wedges the arm silently**

The once-per-head marker makes the ghost re-dispatch strictly one-shot per head: if the fresh CI run the machine dispatches here gets cancelled again (the gh-748 kicker race is not guaranteed to be gone — the incident that spawned this card was a cancel storm), the next tick finds `ghostProbe.isGhostCancel && ghostGateHeld` true, sees the marker, and takes this branch:

```js
console.log('  ⏭️  ' + key + ' ghost-cancelled validation already re-dispatched for head — waiting on the run');
continue;
```

— and waits forever, while the merge gate still refuses (`Required status check "crap" is expected`) and no further action or alarm is ever emitted. That is precisely the permanent-wedge shape this ticket bans, just moved one level down.

The ticket's E3 prescribes "re-dispatch at most once per tick per PR, **with a flap counter and escalating backoff** — the cure must not amplify the race." The once-per-head marker satisfies the rate-limit but has no flap counter and no alarm: after the second cancel there is no visible state, no `mutex_*`-style metric, and no escalation. At minimum, count re-cancels after a machine re-dispatch and emit an alarm record (and consider the Q2 auto-issue channel) once the flap count crosses a threshold — a silent `⏭️` log line is not an acceptable terminal state for a guest PR that can never self-escape.

💡 **SUGGESTION: `PHANTOM_ALARM_CAP` is dead — declared, exported, documented, never used**

```js
var PHANTOM_ALARM_CAP = 3;
```

The docstring on `recordPhantomHeal` says "Alarm records cap at `PHANTOM_ALARM_CAP` per holder signature", but the implementation filters by holder signature and then caps the *total* list at `MAX_ALARMS` (5) — `PHANTOM_ALARM_CAP` never appears in any code path. Either implement the documented per-signature cap (drop the matching-signature entry and keep at most 3 alarms for any one signature) or delete the constant and fix the docstring. As-is it misleads the next reader about the actual cap semantics.

💡 **SUGGESTION: session-local runtime state churned into the PR**

This file is the fa harness's live bash-job registry — a per-session, machine-local state blob (note the embedded absolute paths and PIDs from the authoring machine). `.fah/` is already in `.gitignore`, but this file remains tracked, so every session keeps diffing it into otherwise unrelated PRs (this PR's diff is ~15 KB of it before the real changes begin).

Please restore it to the `main` version (`git checkout origin/main -- .fah/bash_jobs/running.json`) and untrack it (`git rm --cached .fah/bash_jobs/running.json` in a follow-up) so future PRs stop carrying local session noise.

💡 **SUGGESTION: quote the `--ref` value — this path is explicitly built for guest PRs**

```js
command: 'gh workflow run ' + ghostCi +
         ' --repo ' + effectiveRepoInfo.owner + '/' + effectiveRepoInfo.repo +
         ' --ref ' + (ticket.branch || '')
```

The branch name flows unquoted into a shell command, and this code path is by design authorship-blind — it fires for **guest** PRs (the gh-757 restriction covers pushes, not this dispatch), so the interpolated value is guest-controlled. Git ref names permit shell metacharacters (`;`, `&`, `|`, `$()`, backticks), so a crafted branch name could inject into the SM runner's shell (which holds the machine token).

The older dispatch sites in this file share the same pattern, so this is consistency, not a new deviation — but since this PR extends the pattern to a guest-triggered path, please single-quote the ref (`'--ref \\'' + ... + '\\''` or an args-array equivalent if the host tool supports it) here, and ideally track a follow-up to harden the pre-existing sites the same way.

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:

jobs:

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title` and no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

```js
console.log('   ⚠️ ' + alarm.title + ' — ' + alarm.detail + ' (cached holders [' + ...);
```

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

Fix: include `consecutivePhantomTicks: 1` in the event (or call `recordPhantomHeal` at this site as designed), and have the publish step reset the counter to 0 when the current tick carried no phantom event.

The branch name flows unquoted into a shell command, and this code path is by design authorship-blind — it fires for **guest** PRs (the gh-757 restriction covers pushes, not this dispatch), so the interpolated value is guest-controlled. Git ref names permit shell metacharacters (`;`, `&`, `|`, `$()`, backticks), so a crafted branch name could inject into the SM runner's shell (which holds the machine token).

The older dispatch sites in this file share the same pattern, so this is consistency, not a new deviation — but since this PR extends the pattern to a guest-triggered path, please single-quote the ref (`'--ref \\'' + ... + '\\''` or an args-array equivalent if the host tool supports it) here, and ideally track a follow-up to harden the pre-existing sites the same way.

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}

jobs:

    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,

    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

Fix: include `consecutivePhantomTicks: 1` in the event (or call `recordPhantomHeal` at this site as designed), and have the publish step reset the counter to 0 when the current tick carried no phantom event.

Nothing drives a full-slot defer scenario through `queryPrs`'s new phantom-heal branch, and nothing drives `rerun_cancelled_checks`'s new ghost-cancel branch in `smAgent`.

This file is the fa harness's live bash-job registry — a per-session, machine-local state blob (note the embedded absolute paths and PIDs from the authoring machine). `.fah/` is already in `.gitignore`, but this file remains tracked, so every session keeps diffing it into otherwise unrelated PRs (this PR's diff is ~15 KB of it before the real changes begin).

```js
command: 'gh workflow run ' + ghostCi +
```

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \

            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"

          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title` and no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

```js
console.log('   ⚠️ ' + alarm.title + ' — ' + alarm.detail + ' (cached holders [' + ...);
```

So the self-heal alarm — the I2-mandated observable signal that the registry diverged — logs as `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ioCache self-healed, defer cancelled)`. The same `alarm` object is also stored in the factory-state alarm tail, so any consumer rendering `alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` (including future Q2 auto-issue filing on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks) sees the same holes.

Fix: either add `title`/`detail` to the alarm objects in `mutexRegistry.reconcile`/`recordPhantomHeal`, or log `alarm.type` (+ a human-readable phrase) here.

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

Fix: include `consecutivePhantomTicks: 1` in the event (or call `recordPhantomHeal` at this site as designed), and have the publish step reset the counter to 0 when the current tick carried no phantom event.

pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

**Summary**: The heart of the fix is dead in production — `queryPrs`'s phantom-holder self-heal guards on `provider.githubApi('list_prs', …)` but the `smProvider` facade exposes no `githubApi` method, so the live re-read never runs and a phantom holder still wedges the queue (AC2 unmet). The PR description's "no regressions" claim does not hold against this gate.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 Core self-heal unreachable: `provider.githubApi` does not exist on the facade (js/sm/sources/githubSource.js:840)

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title` and no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

```js
console.log('   ⚠️ ' + alarm.title + ' — ' + alarm.detail + ' (cached holders [' + ...);
```

So the self-heal alarm — the I2-mandated observable signal that the registry diverged — logs as `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ioCache self-healed, defer cancelled)`. The same `alarm` object is also stored in the factory-state alarm tail, so any consumer rendering `alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` (including future Q2 auto-issue filing on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks) sees the same holes.

Fix: either add `title`/`detail` to the alarm objects in `mutexRegistry.reconcile`/`recordPhantomHeal`, or log `alarm.type` (+ a human-readable phrase) here.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

Fix: include `consecutivePhantomTicks: 1` in the event (or call `recordPhantomHeal` at this site as designed), and have the publish step reset the counter to 0 when the current tick carried no phantom event.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no test exercises the new wiring — AC2/AC3 integration paths are untested**

Every hunk in this file (and in `test_smAgent.js` / `test_mergeCadence.js`) only adds `'../../common/mutexRegistry.js': loadModule(...)` to the require maps. Nothing drives a full-slot defer scenario through `queryPrs`'s new phantom-heal branch, and nothing drives `rerun_cancelled_checks`'s new ghost-cancel branch in `smAgent`.

This gap is exactly why the BLOCKING `provider.githubApi` defect slipped through: a single test loading `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module (or a stub shaped like its facade) and asserting the live re-read fires on a full-slot defer would have caught that the guard is unsatisfiable in production.

The ticket's test plan explicitly requires these hooks: IT-1 (scripted two-tick phantom self-heal → AC2), IT-2 (cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe → AC3), plus the REG-1 replay rule ("red REG blocks merge of this fix"). This PR ships only pure-function UTs of `mutexRegistry`; the scripted two-tick scenario and the REG fixture are absent. Please add at least the IT-1/IT-2 level tests against the real provider facade shape before merge.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment5.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: session-local runtime state churned into the PR**

This file is the fa harness's live bash-job registry — a per-session, machine-local state blob (note the embedded absolute paths and PIDs from the authoring machine). `.fah/` is already in `.gitignore`, but this file remains tracked, so every session keeps diffing it into otherwise unrelated PRs (this PR's diff is ~15 KB of it before the real changes begin).

Please restore it to the `main` version (`git checkout origin/main -- .fah/bash_jobs/running.json`) and untrack it (`git rm --cached .fah/bash_jobs/running.json` in a follow-up) so future PRs stop carrying local session noise.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment8.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: quote the `--ref` value — this path is explicitly built for guest PRs**

```js
command: 'gh workflow run ' + ghostCi +
         ' --repo ' + effectiveRepoInfo.owner + '/' + effectiveRepoInfo.repo +
         ' --ref ' + (ticket.branch || '')
```

The branch name flows unquoted into a shell command, and this code path is by design authorship-blind — it fires for **guest** PRs (the gh-757 restriction covers pushes, not this dispatch), so the interpolated value is guest-controlled. Git ref names permit shell metacharacters (`;`, `&`, `|`, `$()`, backticks), so a crafted branch name could inject into the SM runner's shell (which holds the machine token).

The older dispatch sites in this file share the same pattern, so this is consistency, not a new deviation — but since this PR extends the pattern to a guest-triggered path, please single-quote the ref (`'--ref \\'' + ... + '\\''` or an args-array equivalent if the host tool supports it) here, and ideally track a follow-up to harden the pre-existing sites the same way.

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

- Split `silentUpdateFailureCount` (110 — the regex-while loop plus counting makes it the worst offender), `mutexHoldersOf` (56), `normalizeHolder` (36.8), `isGhostCancelProbe` (20), `normalizeMutexSnapshot` (20, including its inner `num`).
- `silentUpdateAttemptsLeft: 12` is a one-liner whose score is coverage-driven — it needs a direct unit test.

The PR description's "Full suite … 3603 tests passed, 0 failures, no regressions" is true only for the unit suite; the required CRAP gate is a separate, red merge blocker.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: alarm log line prints `undefined — undefined`**

`mutexRegistry.reconcile()` builds its alarm record as:

```js
var alarm = { type: 'phantom_mutex_holder', label: 'ai_validating', repo: ..., holders: {...}, at: ... };
```

There is no `title` and no `title`/`detail` pair anywhere in the alarm shape (`recordPhantomHeal` builds the same field set). But this line does:

```js
console.log('   ⚠️ ' + alarm.title + ' — ' + alarm.detail + ' (cached holders [' + ...);
```

So the self-heal alarm — the I2-mandated observable signal that the registry diverged — logs as `⚠️ undefined — undefined — (cached holders [5] vs live []; ioCache self-healed, defer cancelled)`. The same `alarm` object is also stored in the factory-state alarm tail, so any consumer rendering `alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` (including future Q2 auto-issue filing on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks) sees the same holes.

Fix: either add `title`/`detail` to the alarm objects in `mutexRegistry.reconcile`/`recordPhantomHeal`, or log `alarm.type` (+ a human-readable phrase) here.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never populated in production and would never reset**

Two compounding defects around the consecutive-phantom counter:

1. **Never fed.** The only production increment comes from this event — but it omits the key:

```js
recordMutexTickEvent({ mutexSelfHeals: 1, phantomHolderTicks: 1, alarm: alarm });
// consecutivePhantomTicks is undefined here ⇒ num() coerces to 0
```

The only function that increments `consecutivePhantomTicks` is `recordPhantomHeal`, which nothing in production calls (only `test_mutexRegistry.js` does). So the published factory-state `mutex.consecutivePhantomTicks` stays `0` forever, and the ticket's Q2 follow-up ("auto-issue on ≥3 consecutive phantom ticks") has no data to key on.

2. **Never reset.** Even if the key were fed, the cross-tick publish merge does `mergeSnapshot(spPrev.mutex, spMutex)` — on a clean tick (`spMutex === null`) the previous value is carried forward unchanged (`prev + 0`), so "consecutive" would accumulate monotonically across unrelated clean ticks instead of resetting to 0.

Fix: include `consecutivePhantomTicks: 1` in the event (or call `recordPhantomHeal` at this site as designed), and have the publish step reset the counter to 0 when the current tick carried no phantom event.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md"}

{"content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: no test exercises the new wiring — AC2/AC3 integration paths are untested**

Every hunk in this file (and in `test_smAgent.js` / `test_mergeCadence.js`) only adds `'../../common/mutexRegistry.js': loadModule(...)` to the require maps. Nothing drives a full-slot defer scenario through `queryPrs`'s new phantom-heal branch, and nothing drives `rerun_cancelled_checks`'s new ghost-cancel branch in `smAgent`.

This gap is exactly why the BLOCKING `provider.githubApi` defect slipped through: a single test loading `githubSource` with the real `smProvider` module (or a stub shaped like its facade) and asserting the live re-read fires on a full-slot defer would have caught that the guard is unsatisfiable in production.

The ticket's test plan explicitly requires these hooks: IT-1 (scripted two-tick phantom self-heal → AC2), IT-2 (cancelled-run re-dispatch with gh-748 dedupe → AC3), plus the REG-1 replay rule ("red REG blocks merge of this fix"). This PR ships only pure-function UTs of `mutexRegistry`; the scripted two-tick scenario and the REG fixture are absent. Please add at least the IT-1/IT-2 level tests against the real provider facade shape before merge.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment5.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: session-local runtime state churned into the PR**

This file is the fa harness's live bash-job registry — a per-session, machine-local state blob (note the embedded absolute paths and PIDs from the authoring machine). `.fah/` is already in `.gitignore`, but this file remains tracked, so every session keeps diffing it into otherwise unrelated PRs (this PR's diff is ~15 KB of it before the real changes begin).

Please restore it to the `main` version (`git checkout origin/main -- .fah/bash_jobs/running.json`) and untrack it (`git rm --cached .fah/bash_jobs/running.json` in a follow-up) so future PRs stop carrying local session noise.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment8.md"}

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: quote the `--ref` value — this path is explicitly built for guest PRs**

```js
command: 'gh workflow run ' + ghostCi +
         ' --repo ' + effectiveRepoInfo.owner + '/' + effectiveRepoInfo.repo +
         ' --ref ' + (ticket.branch || '')
```

The branch name flows unquoted into a shell command, and this code path is by design authorship-blind — it fires for **guest** PRs (the gh-757 restriction covers pushes, not this dispatch), so the interpolated value is guest-controlled. Git ref names permit shell metacharacters (`;`, `&`, `|`, `$()`, backticks), so a crafted branch name could inject into the SM runner's shell (which holds the machine token).

The older dispatch sites in this file share the same pattern, so this is consistency, not a new deviation — but since this PR extends the pattern to a guest-triggered path, please single-quote the ref (`'--ref \\'' + ... + '\\''` or an args-array equivalent if the host tool supports it) here, and ideally track a follow-up to harden the pre-existing sites the same way.

Review complete. **Verdict: REQUEST_CHANGES** — 2 blocking, 4 important, 3 suggestions.

## Summary

**BLOCKING #1 — the core fix is dead in production.** `queryPrs`'s phantom-holder self-heal guards on `provider.githubApi('list_prs', …)`, but the `smProvider` facade exposes no `githubApi` method (verified by exhaustive grep of the facade's full return object). The live label-layer re-read never runs, so a phantom `ai_validating` holder still wedges the queue exactly as in the incident — AC2 ("queued candidate arms in the SAME tick") is unmet. Unit tests pass only because nothing drives this branch with a production-shaped provider.

**BLOCKING #2 — required `crap` CI gate is red** on head commit `1c8008e5` (full log fetched via `gh run view`): `queryPrs` 67.4→131.8 and `buildFactoryState` 65.1→66.1 regressions, plus 10 new functions over the CRAP threshold of 8 (worst: `silentUpdateFailureCount` 110, `mutexHoldersOf` 56, `normalizeHolder` 36.8). The ratchet only ratchets down — the new code must be decomposed; the dead `githubApi` block is also what blew up `queryPrs`'s score.

**Important:** alarm log prints `undefined — undefined` (`alarm.title`/`alarm.detail` are never set by `reconcile`); `consecutivePhantomTicks` is never fed in production (only the test-only `recordPhantomHeal` increments it; the tick event omits the key; the cross-tick merge never resets it); zero tests exercise the new `queryPrs`/`smAgent` wiring (the IT-1/IT-2 scripted scenarios and REG fixture from the test plan are absent); and an E3 gap — if the re-dispatched run is cancelled again, the once-per-head marker suppresses all further retries and the arm re-wedges with only a skip log line.

**Suggestions:** `PHANTOM_ALARM_CAP` is declared/documented but unused; `.fah/bash_jobs/running.json` session state (local paths/PIDs) churned into the diff; unquoted `--ref` shell interpolation on a path explicitly built for guest PRs.
